title: A conformance suite, and a mark that can be withheld
description:
THE FAILURE THIS PREVENTS: the day a second implementation exists, the
word HIRE means whatever its vendor says it means. Without something
executable to point at, "HIRE-compatible" is a marketing claim, and the
first one that ships a lower-quality answer under the same vocabulary
sets the meaning for everyone.

TWO HALVES, AND ONLY THE SECOND IS GOVERNANCE.

1. THE SUITE. Executable, runnable by anyone in minutes, against any
daemon speaking the Workload API. The model already exists in
hire-grpc/tests/stock_client.rs: a third-party client library driven
through connect, fetch, bundle fetch and cryptographic validation. That
test proves OUR conformance to SPIFFE. Inverted, the same shape proves
SOMEONE ELSE's conformance to hire.

The tests that matter are not the ones that check a field is present.
They are the ones that check an implementation cannot say something it
has not established:

* a claim reporting an assurance tier with no evidence behind it fails
* a claim reporting presence with no authenticator assertion behind it
  fails, which is why this is coupled to persona-3tly.1: until the
  assertion reaches the consumer there is nothing for a suite to check,
  and the presence half of conformance cannot be written at all
* an unnamed request that prompts a human fails, because ProofCost::
  Silent is a guarantee rather than a hint
* an unknown hire_ audience parameter that is ignored rather than
  refused fails

2. THE MARK. A conformance suite with no consequence for failing it is a
document. The consequence is the name, and a name can only be withheld
by someone who holds it. Today that is one person, which is exactly as
strong as that person: buyable, suable, mortal. UPSTREAM.md lists
assigning the trademark to the Linux Foundation under what we would be
GIVING UP. Under sudden adoption it is the enforcement mechanism, and
the only reason the suite has teeth.

Note also that UPSTREAM records the name itself is not yet clean:
hire/HiRE is taken on crates.io and github.com/hire is taken. A mark
that cannot be assigned cannot be withheld either.

SEQUENCING. The suite can be written now and is useful immediately as a
second opinion on our own daemon. The mark question is a decision, not a
project, and the cheap version of it is recording which name we intend
to be able to give away.
acceptance_criteria: A suite anyone can run against a daemon claiming to be HIRE, which fails an implementation that reports an assurance or presence level it cannot substantiate; and a decision recorded on who holds the name.
